sections.text: The whole world is pervaded by Me, yet My form is not seen. All living things have their being in Me, yet I am not limited by them.
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्।
Nevertheless, they do not consciously abide in Me. Such is My Divine Sovereignty that though I, the Supreme Self, am the cause and upholder of all, yet I remain outside.
As the mighty wind, though moving everywhere, has no resting place but space, so have all these beings no home but Me.

We had been discussing chapter nine, Rajavidya Rajaguhya Yoga, the royal secret. In the royal knowledge, we have seen up to chapter eight in which we have learned about ourselves -- who we are in this limited self, what is our goal, and how we can evolve out of it. Then we ask, but what do we meditate upon? What do we evolve into? We have said you have to evolve from this limited self, identifying with this limited being, to the infinite self, unlimited being -- and thats you.
Meditate upon whatever we want to achieve, we meditate on that. But unless I know the nature of that infinite self and my relationship with it, how can I meditate upon it? So in chapter eight we have seen imperishable Brahman, that entity which remains in existence all the time. Even when I perish or this world will perish, that substratum which creates this reality will always be there.
So now chapter nine says, what is my relationship with that imperishable Brahman? He is the source, he is the resting place. But what is my relationship with that? And so chapter nine says that is the royal secret. Right now I dont really see any relationship, even though Ive heard through all these scriptures and books and religions.
But I personally cannot feel any relationship with him. So what is my relationship? He said that is the royal secret. You, knowing yourself, do not know what your relationship with yourself is.
That is the deepest secret -- the most secret is that its right there. Looking for my key all the time, and its always in my pocket. That is the biggest secret.
So thats the Raja Guhyam, and Raja Vidya. Knowing this -- knowing how to know this secret -- is the supreme knowledge. Once I realize my key is in my pocket that time I have the joy of my life.
Up till now I was so worried about where is my key, Im going to be late for my meeting and all of that. Suddenly I realized that right here, that is the greatest knowledge I can have at that moment. Anything else, you tell me at that time and say, well let me tell you.
The E is equal to MC square. Look, I know I want my key. So when we get what we want to know is the supreme knowledge.
So Bhagavan said, thats what Im going to tell you in this chapter. So in the first three verses he gave the promise. And now he says, let me tell you what that secret is.
So in verse four he says: Mayatatam idam sarvam jagat avyaktamurtina. I am pervading this Jagat. This entire Jagat, this entire cosmos, this entire universe is pervaded by me in my unmanifest form.
That which is illuminated is Jagat. That which is illuminated by my senses. My Jagat is limited to that.
That which I do not know is not part of my world. So Jagat is that which is illuminated by my senses. Your senses define your Jagat.
Her senses define her Jagat. When you put everyones Jagat together, that is the total Jagat. Bhagavan said, I pervade this entire Jagat, whatever is illuminated by any being in this world.
I pervade that in my unmanifest form. The manifest is something I can say, oh yeah, I have seen it, I have touched it, I have been there. But the unmanifest is something beyond my perception.
So Bhagavan said, this world of your perception is pervaded by me in my unmanifest form. Therefore you see the Jagat but do not see me, because Im unmanifest. But Im always there in anything you perceive, see, touch, or feel.
Here is my nature: your entire Jagat is pervaded by me. In my unmanifest form. That also includes myself -- I can perceive, feel, touch.
But wait, if thats part of your Jagat, then I am pervading through that. In my unmanifest form. My mind -- I can feel my thoughts.
Well then I am pervading in that also in my unmanifest form. My intellect. So then Im also pervading in the unmanifest form.
Matsthani sarva bhutani. At least we understood that Bhagavan says he is in unmanifest form. Whatever you think of, right there, his presence is there.
As long as I can consider something as part of my Jagat, Bhagavan is right there. So now I come to the conclusion: Bhagavan resides in all of them. Thats what all religions tell us.
Bhagavan resides in you. The Lord resides in your heart. So you say, well, lets not get confused here.
Okay, so what is my real nature? Matsthani, sarvabhutani, nacha aham te su avasthitaha. All these beings or things which you see, perceive, touch, and feel as your Jagat -- they reside in me, but I am not in them. See, in the first line he said that he pervades this entire Jagat of yours in his unmanifest form.
We put two and two together and said, therefore he is in all of them. But no -- I am not in them, they are in me. My standard example: I buy a car and take it from Chesterfield County and bring it to Henrico County. What if Chesterfield County claims that the space in Mr.
Batues car was Chesterfield County space? Henrico County, you cant keep it there. Now you have extra space. Please return the extra space -- he took it with his car from Chesterfield County. Can I return that space in my car to Chesterfield County? What happened to the space which was in my car when the car was in Chesterfield County? It remained in Chesterfield County.
When the car came to Henrico County, the space in the car changed from Chesterfield to Henrico. The car moved through the space. So the conundrum is: is the space in the car, or is the car in the space? Obviously, if I cannot return the space from Henrico to Chesterfield -- Oh, here is the extra space I brought with me -- then obviously the car was moving in the space, not the other way around.
So now the space can say, All the cars are in me. But it also says, I am not in them. Now you have the puzzle -- there is no separate space in my car. So Bhagavan says, Matsthani Sarva Bhutani -- all the things and beings you can think of are in me. Your Jagat is whatever you can perceive, feel, think, and touch.
Now everything I see, Bhagavan says he pervades in unmanifest form. In other words, he is not limited to your Jagat. If I only say that Bhagavan pervades the entire Jagat, I know the Jagat in manifest form, and Bhagavan is in unmanifest form.
The law of conservation says, in this world there is always the same amount of energy and matter. Whether its in a form of a matter, form of energy. The total energy remains the same at any given time.
So I can say, okay, the Bhagavan says he is unmanifest. So if I put sum it up, all the parts of my Jagat I know the Bhagavan. I say, no, they are in me, but I am not in them.
I am something beyond that. So he said, what is that relationship then? So is that its a relationship less relations. Just as the space in the car and the space outside.
Theres really no relationship to the car. Its not because the car is here. There is a space here.
The car will move, the space will move. With is my perception that the space is in the car. Space was always here outside this door.
When I brought my car and parked it, I perceived that space is in my car. Space never moved from anywhere to anywhere. In a similar way, the classical example we learn in Vedanta is that of a snake and a rope.
The existence of snake is very real. Is part of my Jagat, my world. When I see a snake, I perceive it.
I can vouch for it that there is a snake here. And therefore it is part of my Jagat. Now Bhagavan said, in unmanifest form, the rope was existing while I was seeing the snake in it.
That snake could not have come into existence without the existence of the rope. So now the rope can say that I was always pervading through this entire snake in my unmanifest form while you were seeing the snake in me. Therefore the snake is in me.
But I as the rope am not in the snake. The rope has no relationship to the snake whatsoever. Snake cannot exist without that rope.
But it takes the support of my ignorance, my perception. My perception created snake in my Jagat in my world. Because Jagat is only limited by my perception.
That which I can illumine as world of plurality is my Jagat. Snake was part of my Jagat. Without the rope, the snake could not have existed.
And therefore rope was existing in its unmanifest form in the snake all the time. But it was never in the snake. Bhagavan said, all these beings are existing in me.
In other words, without my existence, there is no existence for anything. Therefore they are in me. But I, in my pristine nature, unlimited, formless, was never in any of these shapes and forms and colors which you see.
So the next verse takes it further -- in case you think we got it all. Nachamatsthani Bhutani, Pashya Me Yogam Aishvaram, Bhuta Bhrit Na Cha Bhutastho Mamatma Bhuta Bhavanaha. Now he says that all these beings exist in me because we have seen the snake exists in the rope.
But the rope is not existing in the snake. So now you think okay, the beings are in him. But then he adds: these beings are also not existing in me.
The beings which I am perceiving, seeing, touching, and feeling are part of my Jagat. But the Brahman who is pervading all this Jagat has nothing to do with that. The snake which was existing in the rope -- the rope can say, It existed in me, but I am not in them. But now he goes further.
If we think we got it correct and say, Okay, so the snake was always in the rope, he says, no -- Nachamatsthani Bhutani. Even though these beings are existing in me, there was never a time -- from the perspective of the one who knew the rope -- that the snake was existing in that rope. In my world there was a snake.
But the next guy standing with his torchlight, who at least knew that its a rope -- for him, there was no snake in his Jagat. The snake was only possible because of the rope, yet from his perspective, there was no snake ever in the rope. So in reality, there is never a snake existing in the rope.
The rope remained rope all the time -- before I created the snake in it and after I realized there is no snake. Therefore Bhagavan says: in your Jagat, you create this world through your perception. You create this world of plurality -- I exist, you exist, she exists, he exists.
And now I said, I am the center of my universe. The world revolves around me. You are in the center of your universe and the world revolves around you.
So from my perspective, in my Jagat, beings exist. Because the Supreme Being exist. And that being pervades through all the beings in my Jagat.

All beings dwell in Me, but I do not dwell in them (matsthani sarvabhutani na caham tesvavasthitah) - this paradox holds the key to understanding our relationship with the Divine. Like space that appears to be in a car but actually contains the car, we exist within the infinite consciousness, not the other way around. The space doesnt move when the car travels from one county to another - the car moves through unchanging space. Similarly, your true Self remains unchanging while the body-mind moves through experiences.
The analogy of the snake and rope illuminates this further: the snake (this world of multiplicity) cannot exist without the rope (Brahman), yet from the ropes perspective, no snake ever existed. Your limitations, your problems, your separate identity - these exist in the Divine like the snake exists in the rope. They are real to your perception but have no fundamental reality. This is the relationless relationship - we are intimately connected to the Divine (closer than close), yet the Divine remains untouched by our perceived limitations.
Contemplation for today: When you look at any object or person, remind yourself: This exists in consciousness, not consciousness in this. Notice how this shifts your sense of what is fundamental and what is derivative. Where you once saw solid, separate objects, begin to sense the unmanifest presence that pervades and supports all that you perceive.
